title: Introduce invocation slimline metrics and log anchoring
author: Aisha Patel
description: Motivation: customers want lightweight per-invocation signals for alerting and perf triage without the overhead of full-span hydration. This PR adds a slimline metric set (compact counters/histograms) emitted at the invocation boundary together with a small log-anchoring protocol that lets sampled traces pull the most relevant log snippets for quick RCA. Goals: 1) provide low-cardinality, high-signal invocation metrics that fit retention/ingestion budgets; 2) enable cheap, deterministic linkage between a metric-level anomaly and a small, developer-friendly log excerpt; 3) preserve existing tracing semantics and sampling decisions. What is included: - invocation_slimline metrics: invocation.count, invocation.error_rate, invocation.latency_slab, invocation.token_delta (per-100-token buckets), invocation.hotpath_flag. Metrics are emitted by the serving runtime at the finalization step to avoid double-counting and to be robust to retries. - log anchoring protocol: lightweight anchor tokens are attached to metric emits and to a small log cache. When a metric indicates an anomaly, the UI can request anchored log excerpts for the failed invocation id. Anchors are short, reversible tokens (not secrets) and include minimal context (route, model_version, anchor_ts). - Sampling and retention: default sampler keeps 0.5% of invocations fully hydrated, with a burst window to 5% for detected anomalies. Slimline metrics are always emitted (low cardinality) and designed for long retention. - Dashboard assets: an invocation-timeline dashboard to visualize slimline histograms, hotpath markers, and anchored log excerpts. - Docs and runbook: README and runbook for oncall explaining how to interpret slimline signals and how to initiate an anchored log fetch. Design notes: - Kept metric labels minimal: tenant_id (sharded), model_family, route, stage. No free-form prompt content. - Anchors are stored in a bounded in-memory LRU cache on each arena for up to 60s; archival copies flow to the log-archiver for longer retention if requested by the user. - Backwards compatibility: if the anchoring module is disabled, only slimline metrics emit; no tracing changes required. Checklist: - [x] Implementation of slimline metric emissary in runtime finalizer - [x] Anchoring token generator and cache with eviction policy - [x] End-to-end integration test + unit tests for sampler thresholds - [x] Dashboard JSON and Grafana panels - [x] Docs and runbook - [x] Perf validation: <1% p95 latency add on microbench harness Migration/rollout: feature gated behind observability.feature_slimline. Default off for customers on Dedicated; rollout staged for hosted customers. Operational knobs exposed: slimline.sampling_rate, anchor.cache_size, anchor.ttl_seconds. Related: this PR complements ENG-2312 (contextual cost explorer) and ENG-2356 (alert-weighted sampling). The description of changed files, commits, and reviews below contain implementation details and rationale.

release_notes: Add 'slimline' per-invocation metrics and a log-anchoring mechanism to improve low-cost observability and fast RCA. Opt-in feature behind observability.feature_slimline. See docs/observability/slimline_metrics.md for usage and runbook.
notes_on_rollback: Rollback: flip observability.feature_slimline to false; purge anchor caches across arenas via admin API. No data migration required for metrics; anchored logs in cache will expire.
testing_summary: Unit tests cover sampler thresholds and eviction; e2e harness validates <1% latency overhead on p95 for a 1000qps workload. Integration tests exercised anchor fetch flow and UI panel rendering with mocked log excerpts.
performance_summary: Benchmarks (microbench harness) show median latency change <0.2ms and p95 change <1% with default sampling. Emitting slimline metrics increases cardinality by 4 labels but uses low-cardinality design and sharding to keep ingestion costs modest.
observability_guidance: Oncall runbook: - If invocation.count spikes with error_rate increase, open anchored log for top routes; use sampler.boost to capture a wider window. - Use invocation.token_delta histogram to assess prompt/response token cost shifts. - Hotpath_flag marks requests that touched fallback models or retried KV cache misses. - If false positives observed, lower sampler.boost_window_seconds or increase anomaly threshold.
